text: Well, well. Another O'Brien looking for a key.
Sully told me you might come by.
Hi, uh, sorry to bother you. I'm Danny. Sully's nephew? Great-nephew? Something like that.
Let's skip the small talk. I'm Colleen. You have something I need.
The name's Fitz. And before you ask — yes, I know about the tunnels under the city.
Meg. Here for the key. Can we make this quick?
Let's see if you know your Boston. Five questions. Get three right.
Ah, you must be one of Sully's. Got his stubborn look about you.
He said if anyone came asking, they better earn it.
That sounds like him. I'm Danny. I, uh, hope I don't disappoint.
Colleen. And I don't plan on asking — I plan on taking.
Fitz. Sully once told me this bar has a hidden basement. Is that true?
Meg. And I'm already tired. Let's do this.
Alright, hotshot. Five questions about this neighborhood. Miss more than two, you're out.
Hold on. You look familiar. You related to Sully?
He used to come in here every Tuesday. Miss that old bastard.
I'm Danny. His great-nephew. Or nephew once removed? I never figured it out.
Colleen. His niece. And I'd rather not get sentimental about it.
Fitz. Did you know Sully had a secret safe deposit box at three different banks?
Meg. And yeah, I miss him too. But I'm here for the key, not therapy.
You want what Sully left you? Prove you deserve it. Five questions.
Not bad, kid. Not bad at all.
Sully would've been proud. Here's your key.
Huh. You actually know your stuff.
Sully always said his family wasn't completely hopeless. Guess he was right.
Well, look at that. An O'Brien who can answer questions.
Here. You earned this. Don't lose it.
That's... not great.
You want another shot? Redemption challenge?
Ooh. Sully's probably rolling in his grave.
Look, I'll give you one more chance. Different kind of test.
That was painful to watch.
Tell you what — there's another way. You game?
You're here about Sully's thing, aren't you?
He mentioned family might come looking. Didn't say when.
Yes sir. I'm Danny. Sully was my... actually, I'm not sure what he was to me.
Colleen. And I don't have time for stories about the old days.
Fitz. Did Sully ever mention anything about the 1919 molasses flood being an inside job?
Meg. And whatever you're about to tell me about Sully, I've probably heard it.
You want my key? Show me you know the North End. Five questions.
Ah, another one. Sully had a lot of relatives, eh?
Some of them already came through. You're not the first.
Wait, others came already? I'm Danny, by the way. Did I miss something?
Colleen. And I don't care who came before me. I care who leaves with the key.
Fitz. Who else came? Were they asking about the tunnels?
Meg. Great. Competition. Just what I needed.
Same rules for everyone. Five questions about my neighborhood.
You got Sully's eyes. He used to sit right there, you know.
Ordered the same thing every time. Capicola sandwich, extra peppers.
That sounds like him. I'm Danny. I, uh, never actually had capicola.
Colleen. And I'm not here for sandwiches.
Fitz. Was that sandwich a code? Did Sully leave messages in his food orders?
Meg. Sounds delicious. Can we do this?
If you want his key, you gotta prove you know this place. Ready?
Bene, bene. You know your history.
Sully chose well. The key is yours.
Not bad for an O'Brien. Most of them can't tell penne from rigatoni.
Here. Don't make me regret this.
You passed. Sully would've bought you a drink.
Take the key. And come back sometime for that sandwich.
Mamma mia. That was rough.
Look, I'll give you another chance. Different test.
You sure you're related to Sully? He knew everything.
One more shot. Redemption round.
Eh, we've all had bad days.
Try again? Different challenge this time.
You look lost. This ain't the tourist section.
Wait — you're one of Sully's, aren't you? He said someone might show up.
Yeah, I'm Danny. Sully's... relative. Sorry, I'm not good with titles.
Colleen. And I know exactly where I am.
Fitz. Did Sully ever tell you about the curse on the Red Sox that wasn't actually a curse?
Meg. And I'm here for the key, not a game.
You want Sully's key? Prove you know Fenway. Five questions.
Ah, another O'Brien coming out of the woodwork.
Sully always said his family would fight over his stuff. Guess he was right.
I'm not trying to fight anyone. I'm Danny. Just want to help settle things.
Colleen. And I don't fight. I win.
Fitz. Fighting implies equal opponents. I prefer the term 'informed competition.'
Meg. And I'm not fighting. I'm just... tired of all of this.
Same deal Sully made with me. Answer my questions, get the key.
Hold up. I know that look. You're Sully's people.
He came to every game he could. Knew more about this park than the groundskeepers.
I'm Danny. Sully tried to teach me about baseball once. It didn't stick.
Colleen. I don't care about baseball. I care about the key.
Fitz. Did you know Fenway has seventeen secret rooms? Sully showed me one.
Meg. I know more than I look like I know. Let's get this over with.
Five questions. Miss more than two, you're walking away empty.
Hot damn! You actually know your stuff!
Sully would've bought you a beer. Here's your key.
Well, well. An O'Brien who knows their Sox.
Take it. You earned it.
I'm impressed. Most people can't name the Monster's height.
Key's yours. Don't spend it all in one place.
Ouch. That hurt to watch.
Look, I'll give you a second chance. Different kind of test.
Sully's spinning in his grave right now.
Tell you what — one more shot. Redemption style.
That was... not great.
You want to try again? I've got another challenge for you.
Oh, wonderful. Another one of Sully's projects.
He always did love his little treasure hunts.
Hi, I'm Danny. You must be... someone important?
Colleen. And I'm not a project. I'm here for what's mine.
Fitz. The State House has thirty-seven hidden passages. Did you know that?
Meg. And can we skip the attitude? I've had a long day.
Fine. Let's see if you're as sharp as Sully thought. Five questions.
Let me guess. You're here about Sully's inheritance.
He always was dramatic. Could've just left a normal will.
I'm Danny. And yeah, the whole key thing is... a lot.
Colleen. Dramatic or not, I'm playing the game he set up.
Fitz. Normal wills are boring. This is much more interesting.
Meg. Tell me about it. I just want this over with.
Well, if you want my key, you'll have to earn it. Five questions about Beacon Hill.
Ah. Sully sent you, didn't he? From beyond the grave.
That man never could do anything the simple way.
I'm Danny. And no, he definitely could not.
Colleen. And I didn't come for commentary on my dead relative.
Fitz. Simple ways are for people without secrets to protect.
Meg. Yeah, well. Here we are anyway.
Show me you know this neighborhood. Then we'll talk about the key.
Well. Color me surprised.
Sully always said his family had potential. Take the key.
I stand corrected. You actually know things.
Here. Don't make me regret giving this to you.
Impressive. Maybe you are worth Sully's trouble.
The key is yours. Use it wisely.
That was disappointing, but not surprising.
I'll give you one more chance. A different kind of test.
Oh dear. Sully overestimated you.
Lucky for you, I believe in second chances. Try this instead.
Well, that was underwhelming.
Redemption round? It's your only option.
You Sully's?
Figured someone would show up eventually.
Yeah. I'm Danny. Nice to meet you.
Colleen. You have a key. I need it.
Fitz. Did Sully ever mention the Brink's job to you?
Meg. And same to you.
Five questions. Charlestown. Don't embarrass yourself.
Another O'Brien. Great.
Sully talked about his family. A lot.
I'm Danny. Hope he said good things?
Colleen. I don't care what he said. I care about the key.
Fitz. What exactly did he say? I'm collecting information.
Meg. Whatever he said, it's probably exaggerated.
Same rules for everyone. Five questions. Ready?
Hmm.
Sully said you'd come. Eventually.
Danny. And... yeah. Here I am.
Colleen. Let's make this quick.
Fitz. How long has 'eventually' been, exactly?
Meg. Better late than never, I guess.
Know Charlestown? Prove it. Five questions.
Not bad.
Key's yours. Sully'd be happy.
You passed.
Here. Don't lose it.
Huh. You actually know things.
Take it. Earned it.
Rough.
One more chance. Different test.
Could've been worse. Could've been better.
Try again?
Sully would've done better.
Redemption round. Yes or no?
Ah, a visitor! Do come in. I'm Miles Ashworth.
Sully — dear old Sully — mentioned family might call.
Hi, I'm Danny. This place is... really nice.
Colleen. And I'm not here to admire the decor.
Fitz. I know your real name is Mickey. From Southie. 1987.
Meg. Nice accent. Very convincing.
Shall we test your knowledge of Back Bay? Five questions ought to suffice.
Welcome, welcome! You have the look of an O'Brien about you.
Sully was a... unique individual. Helped me with some matters once.
I'm Danny. Sully was definitely... unique.
Colleen. I don't need his life story. I need the key.
Fitz. What 'matters'? I'm very interested in matters.
Meg. We've all got our histories. Where's the key?
I'll need some assurance you're worthy. Five questions about the neighborhood.
My, my. The O'Brien clan certainly keeps busy.
Sully warned me there might be... competition.
I'm Danny. And yeah, apparently my whole family wants this bar.
Colleen. Competition just means I need to move faster.
Fitz. Competition is what keeps life interesting. Also conspiracies.
Meg. Great. More pressure. Just what I needed.
Well then. Let's not waste time. Five questions about Back Bay.
Splendid! Absolutely splendid!
Sully chose well. Here is your key.
I must say, I'm impressed.
You've earned this. Take it with my compliments.
Bravo! You know your Boston.
The key is yours. Sully would approve.
Oh dear. That was... unfortunate.
Perhaps a different sort of challenge would suit you better?
Well, that didn't go as hoped, did it?
I'll offer you one more chance. A redemption round.
Hmm. Not quite up to snuff, I'm afraid.
But I'm a fair man. Try again?
You must be one of Sully's. He described your family in... colorful terms.
An interesting man, Sully. We had many debates about the nature of inheritance.
I'm Danny. And yeah, we're a colorful bunch.
Colleen. I didn't come for philosophy. I came for a key.
Fitz. Did you debate the nature of secret societies too?
Meg. I'm sure those debates were riveting. Key, please.
Very well. Let's test your knowledge. Five questions about Cambridge.
Ah, another seeker of Sully's legacy.
He was quite adamant about his... unconventional will.
I'm Danny. Unconventional is one word for it.
Colleen. Unconventional or not, I'm here to win.
Fitz. Unconventional methods often hide deeper truths.
Meg. Yeah. It's definitely that.
Show me you understand this place. Five questions.
Interesting. Sully said his family was... spirited.
He meant it as a compliment, I believe.
I'm Danny. Spirited is generous.
Colleen. I prefer 'determined.'
Fitz. Spirited implies possession. Fascinating word choice.
Meg. Spirited is one way to put it.
Well then. Let's see what you know. Five questions about Cambridge.
Excellent! A mind worth its salt.
Sully would be pleased. The key is yours.
Impressive reasoning and recall.
You've earned this. Take it.
Well done. Knowledge is its own reward, but here's another.
The key. Use it wisely.
Hmm. That was... not your best effort.
Perhaps a different approach? A redemption challenge?
Knowledge gaps are natural. Learning is lifelong.
Try again with a different test?
We all have areas to improve.
I'll give you another chance. Ready?
So you're one of the kids going after Sully's bar.
He always did love making things complicated.
I'm Danny. And yeah, complicated is right.
Colleen. I'm not a kid, and I'm not going after anything. I'm taking it.
Fitz. Complicated systems often hide the most interesting secrets.
Meg. And I'm just tired of the whole thing, honestly.
You want the key? Show me you know Dorchester. Five questions.
Another O'Brien. We keep multiplying.
Sully used to joke we'd take over Boston someday. Maybe he wasn't joking.
I'm Danny. Taking over anything sounds exhausting.
Colleen. I'd settle for taking over that bar.
Fitz. World domination starts with local real estate. Interesting.
Meg. Boston has enough O'Briens. I just want this done.
Same rules Sully set. Five questions. Ready?
Look at you. You've got his nose.
Sully always was my favorite brother. Don't tell the others.
I'm Danny. And... I won't tell.
Colleen. Family secrets aren't my concern. The key is.
Fitz. Secrets are always my concern. What else aren't you telling?
Meg. Your secret's safe. Now about that key...
Sully wanted you to earn it. Five questions about Dorchester.
Well, what do you know. You actually know things.
Sully would've liked that. Here's your key.
Not bad at all. Better than most O'Briens.
Take the key. You earned it.
Impressive. You might actually win this thing.
Here. Don't tell the others I said that.
Oh, honey. That was rough.
But family gets second chances. Try this instead.
Sully would've cringed at that.
Lucky for you, I'm generous. Redemption round?
That could've gone better.
One more shot. Different challenge. You in?
Well, well. An O'Brien in the wild.
Sully used to stop by my corner. Said my poems reminded him of his father.
I'm Danny. That's... really nice, actually.
Colleen. Sweet story. Key, please.
Fitz. Poems often contain hidden messages. Did his?
Meg. Sully had good taste. About the key though...
You want what Sully left? Tell me you know Downtown. Five questions.
Ah, another verse in the O'Brien saga.
Sully's story isn't finished. You're writing the next chapter.
I'm Danny. That's a nice way to put it.
Colleen. I prefer action to metaphors.
Fitz. Every chapter contains clues to the finale. What clues did Sully leave?
Meg. I just want to finish this chapter and go home.
The verse you write depends on what you know. Five questions.
You've got Sully's eyes. Full of questions.
He always asked questions. Never stopped asking.
I'm Danny. And I've got a lot of questions right now.
Colleen. I have one question. Where's the key?
Fitz. Questions are the beginning of all knowledge. What did Sully ask you?
Meg. I'm more answers than questions. Usually.
Now I'll ask the questions. Five of them. About Downtown.
Now that's poetry. Knowledge flowing like verse.
Sully's key is yours. Write something good with it.
Beautiful. You know your history.
Take the key. Sully would've applauded.
Like a perfect rhyme. Everything in its place.
Here's your key. Make the next verse count.
That was more free verse than structured poem.
But every draft can be revised. Try this challenge instead.
The rhythm was off. The meter was broken.
One more chance to find your flow. Ready?
Even the best poets have rough drafts.
Redemption round. Show me what you've really got.
You found me. Sully said you would, eventually.
The last key. The hardest one. Are you ready?
I'm Danny. And I hope so.
Colleen. I've been ready since the first key.
Fitz. Ready is relative. But I'm prepared.
Meg. Let's find out if I'm ready.
The Seaport is new Boston meeting old. Five questions. No mercy.
The final stop. Sully's last test.
He trusted you to get this far. Don't disappoint him now.
I'm Danny. I'll try not to.
Colleen. Disappointment isn't in my vocabulary.
Fitz. Trust is earned through knowledge. I've collected plenty.
Meg. I've come too far to fail now.
Final test. Five questions about the Seaport. Give it everything.
So close now. One key left.
Sully picked me for a reason. This won't be easy.
I'm Danny. Nothing about this has been easy.
Colleen. Easy is boring anyway.
Fitz. Easy answers hide shallow truths. I prefer depth.
Meg. Easy was never the point, was it?
Five questions. The hardest ones yet. Ready?
You did it. The last key.
Sully would be so proud. Now finish what he started.
Impressive. All the way to the end.
Take it. You've earned everything that comes next.
The final piece. You actually made it.
Sully's legacy is in good hands.
So close. But not quite there.
One more chance. The redemption challenge. It's your only shot.
This close to the end... and stumbling.
Sully would give you another try. So will I.
You've come too far to fail here.
Redemption round. Make it count.
